scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Shalako is a series of dances and ceremonies conducted by the Native American Zuni people for the Zuni people at the winter solstice, typically following the harvest.
The Shalako ceremony and feast has been closed to non-native peoples since 1990.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Conducted at the winter solstice following the harvest, the Shalakos bring good fortune, abundant crops, and many children.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Each kiva selects two men, one to portray one of the six Shalakos, and one who alternates in the role, the Shalako Anuthlona.
They appear after the Council of the Gods complete their journey around the village at dusk.
They approach the village from the south, coming down Greasy Hill.
on_screen: Formation: Approach from the south, coming down Greasy Hill, entering designated houses

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Chants are learned by the participants starting at the Winter Solstice and are recited during the early December ceremony, recounting the creation of the Zuni and their search for the Middle.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Shulawitsi is portrayed by a young boy carrying cedar bark torches to light preparatory fires.
The Shalako figures approach from the south, coming down Greasy Hill to enter designated houses in the Zuni village.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The ceremony involves the Koyemshi (father Awan Tatchu and nine offspring), the Council of the Gods including Shulawitsi, Shulawatsi An Tatchu, Saiyatasha, Hututu, Yamuhakto, and the Salimopia Warriors of the Six Directions.
An indigenous American dance and Zuni ceremonial dance tradition.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The Shalako ceremony and feast has been closed to non-native peoples since 1990, and outsiders may only attend if invited by a Zuni tribal member.

scenes.title: Until next time
narration: At the winter solstice, the Zuni people enact the sacred Shalako ceremony, bringing good fortune and creation chants to their village.
